correctness.rationale: For each q>1 and 0<z<1/2 all equilibria are strictly interior and exhaustively rationally parameterized by r in (0,q^-2) union (1,infinity). Algebra verifies the ODE identities and the two physically admissible branches. Strict monotonicity of the high-r branch and a strictly decreasing quartic derivative on the low-r branch give the exact unique fold and counts. Jacobian trace is strictly negative and determinant equals -(q²r²-1) E_q(r)/D_q(r)², establishing all local types and the one-zero-eigenvalue fold. An explicit nonzero second derivative isolates a quadratic fold. Pointwise denominator monotonicity proves strict quality-threshold monotonicity; uniform asymptotic control proves limits. The standalone program executed 126 tests of symbolic identities and sampled full Jacobian eigenvalues; finite tests are corroboration, not universal proof.

value.rationale: The motivating decision system exhibits a metastable inferior consensus for finite quality advantage; the exact sharp zealot boundary and global physical equilibrium classification quantify precisely where the deterministic inferior stable state disappears. The quartic threshold, strict comparative statics and 1/(4q²) quality scaling provide a motivated phase diagram not supplied by the existing qualitative simulations. This is a meaningful model-specific structural result without claiming new observation of bistability, global convergence or swarm-policy efficacy.
